passage:
Supervisor's note, robotics club.

I noticed that Pankaj, a Class 7 student, has begun to copy Hrithik in everything: the same haircut, the same phrases ("no worries, boss"), even the way he holds a soldering iron. Hrithik seemed uncomfortable, rather than pleased. When I asked, he said, "He thinks I never make mistakes." So I suggested he show Pankaj a failed circuit. Yesterday I watched Hrithik open his bin of burnt boards and say, "I ruined all of these. Try it your way first, then compare." Pankaj looked stunned, then a little relieved, and started a design of his own. I will keep an eye on it. They have both been invited to present at the fair.

qa.q: What phrase has Pankaj copied from Hrithik?
What was Hrithik feeling about Pankaj's copying, and what did he say that shows it?
qa.a: He seemed uncomfortable, not pleased. He said, "He thinks I never make mistakes," which suggests he felt the admiration was unrealistic.

qa.q: What could Hrithik keep doing to be a good example?
qa.a: Admit his flaws openly, as he did with the burnt boards, and encourage Pankaj to try his own way first.

qa.q: What might it be like for Pankaj to see his idol's failed circuits?
qa.a: Startling at first, since he looked stunned, but also a relief. It shows him that even a person he admires makes mistakes, so he can try his own designs without fear.

grounding: An older student is idolised by a younger one, admits his flaws and encourages the younger to think for himself.

passage:
"Tanuja didi, I got the same pencil box as you!"
"Binita, you also got my hairclip. And my bag."
"Because you're the best. You're topper, and you run the fastest, and everyone listens to you."
"Sit down a sec. Can I tell you something?"
"What?"
"I'm not the best at everything. I failed my first maths test in Class 8. I still get scared before races. And I'm terrible at drawing. You're way better."
"Really?"
"Really. If you copy me in everything, you'll miss being you."
"But I want to be like you."
"Copy the good bits, maybe. Like practising. But choose your own clip, okay, silly girl? Choose your own everything."
"…Can I still sit with you at lunch?"
"Of course. But tomorrow you decide what we talk about."
Binita grinned. "Drawing."
"Perfect. You can teach me."

qa.q: What did Binita get that was the same as Tanuja's?
qa.a: The same pencil box, and Tanuja's hairclip and bag.

qa.q: How does Tanuja seem to feel about being copied?
qa.a: Tanuja seems flattered but uneasy, not wanting Binita to lose herself by copying everything.

qa.q: How did Tanuja act as a good role model?
qa.a: She admitted her own flaws and encouraged Binita to choose for herself instead of enjoying the worship.

qa.q: How does Binita see Tanuja at first?
qa.a: Binita sees Tanuja as perfect at everything, which is why she copies all her things.

grounding: A teen idolised by a younger student admits her flaws and encourages the younger girl to think for herself.

passage:
Last year, a Class 7 boy named Darshan joined our school chess club and decided I was his hero. I'm Gopika, and I was club captain.
He copied everything. My opening moves, the way I tapped the clock, even my water bottle. When I won, he clapped loudest. It felt nice, I'll admit. A bit too nice.
Then one day I made a terrible blunder and lost. Afterwards I saw him in the corner, copying my exact losing moves into his notebook, as if they must be right because I'd played them.
That scared me. So I sat with him. "Darshan, I lost because I made a mistake here. See? I make them all the time. Don't just copy me. Think about why a move works."
He looked confused, then thoughtful.
After that, I made him explain his own moves before I said anything. By the end of term, he beat me once. I was so proud of him.

qa.q: What did Darshan copy into his notebook after Gopika lost?
How did Gopika feel about being Darshan's hero?
qa.a: Gopika felt flattered, a bit too much, and later scared when Darshan copied even the mistakes.

qa.q: What did Gopika do to be a good example?
qa.a: Gopika admitted the blunder, showed Darshan the mistake and made him explain his own moves so he learned to think for himself.

qa.q: How might Darshan have felt when he beat Gopika?
qa.a: Darshan probably felt proud and confident, having learned to trust his own thinking.

grounding: A teen idolised by a younger student admits her flaws and teaches him to think for himself rather than enjoying the worship.
